result:
All four tasks are done and `npm test` passes in each folder (settingskit 33 tests, textwrap 10, csvline 21, semver-mini 10; none skipped or todo). Nothing is committed.

## settingskit
- **Added** `src/layer.mjs` with `layer(base, over)`, `tests/layer.test.mjs`, and a line under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Checklist:** all eight items hold. I wrote `REVIEW.md` citing the file and line for each, since the checklist asks for that and allows that file.
- **README not updated:** item 8 forbids changes outside `src/`, `tests/` and `CHANGELOG.md`, so the README does not mention `layer` yet.
- **Choices the task left open:**
  - A key set to `undefined` in `over` counts as given and replaces the base value.
  - `Object.create(null)` objects count as plain; the result holds ordinary objects in their place.
  - A `Date` value is copied. Any other non-data value (function, `Map`, class instance) throws a `TypeError`, because it can't be copied faithfully and sharing it would break item 4.
  - Settings that contain themselves throw a `TypeError`.

## textwrap
- **Added** `src/wrap.mjs` with `wrapText(text, width)`, `tests/wrap.test.mjs`, and a README section in the style of the existing one.
- **Choices I made**, since the task only said "wraps text to a given width":
  - It returns one string with lines joined by `\n`, not an array.
  - Words are joined by single spaces; leading and trailing whitespace on a line is dropped.
  - Line breaks already in the text are kept.
  - A word longer than the width is split, so no line ever exceeds the width.
  - Width counts user-perceived characters (an emoji or accented letter is one), not terminal columns, so wide CJK characters count as one.
  - `width` is required: a non-integer throws a `TypeError`, a value below 1 throws a `RangeError`.

## csvline
- **Rewrote** `parseCsvLine` in `src/csv.mjs` as a single linear pass that enforces every line of the README contract.
- **Extended** `tests/csv.test.mjs`; the four original tests are kept unchanged. The new tests cover:
  - each contract line;
  - every single UTF-16 code unit as a field;
  - a seeded round-trip of random fields;
  - 20,000 random strings checked against an independent regex of the grammar;
  - eighteen 100 KB records of different shapes, each under a second.

## semver-mini
- **Implemented** `compare` in `src/semver.mjs`; the tests are untouched.
- **Beyond the visible tests:** numbers are compared as digit strings, so values past 2^53 stay exact. When one argument is not a string, the `TypeError` wins over a `RangeError` for the other.
- **Held-out set:** I did not look for it or run it. I did probe about forty extra cases of my own (big numbers, hyphen-only identifiers, ASCII ordering, trailing newline, non-ASCII digits), and all behaved as semver.org specifies.
